title: atomic KV reconcile and lazy kernel swap to reduce expensive full-fallbacks
author: Asha Menon
description: Context: We observed intermittent large tail latency spikes when the KV cache reconciliation path triggered a full-model fallback (reloading a different kernel or quantized variant) while a continuous-batching hot-path was in flight. Root cause analysis pointed to two issues: (1) non-atomic updates to per-shard KV metadata could cause in-flight requests to see inconsistent cache schemas and take an expensive fallback; (2) the kernel selector eagerly swapped to a compatible kernel on metadata drift even for small, transient inconsistencies, which caused expensive reinitialization and GPU kernel recompile churn. Motivation: reduce tail latency and unnecessary kernel swaps without sacrificing correctness or safety guarantees. Goals: (a) make KV metadata reconcile operations atomic from the runtime request path perspective; (b) introduce a conservative "lazy kernel swap" mode that defers kernel variant activation until the next safe boundary (idle or low-concurrency window) and allows a temporary compatibility shim for in-flight requests; (c) preserve correctness and deterministic outputs for pinned model versions and provide observability to detect deferred swaps. Summary of changes: - runtime/kv_cache/reconciler.go: introduce atomic reconcile operation that stages metadata in a shadow copy, validates schema compatibility across shards, and then atomically flips a reconciliation pointer visible to request handlers. This prevents partial visibility during reconcile. - runtime/kernel_selector.cc/.h: add lazy_swap flag and compatibility shim layer that presents a runtime-accessible adapter when a swap is deferred; the shim forwards most calls but routes tensor allocations through the active kernel until the swap completes. - runtime/scheduler.*: add low-contention window detection and a coordinated swap coordinator that schedules deferred swaps during low concurrency. Also added metrics for deferred_swap_attempts, swap_defer_duration_seconds and reconcile_failures. - runtime/continuous_batcher.py: when atomic reconcile is in flight, the continuous batcher attaches a readonly view of the KV layer so ongoing batches do not see inconsistent entries. Batches are paused (at most 2ms) when a critical reconcile failure is detected. - tests/e2e/batching/kv_reconcile_flow_test.py: end-to-end harness to reproduce prior tail-case and validate new behavior under varied concurrency and request shapes. - docs/notes/kv-reconcile.md: design note and rollout guidance. Commits: - 1a6f3d1: atomic KV reconcile implementation, reconciliation shadow copy and pointer flip - 2b9ecc7: lazy kernel swap scaffolding and compatibility shim - 3c4b9a2: coordinated swap coordinator and low-contention detector - aab0d5f: batcher readonly view + small pause logic - f8e92b1: e2e tests and CI harness + docs Rationale and tradeoffs: - Correctness: the reconcile flip is atomic for request handlers; we preserve deterministic outputs by never mutating visible KV state mid-request. The compatibility shim ensures in-flight batches complete against the kernel they started with. - Performance: lazy swaps reduce recompile/reinit churn and eliminate many full fallbacks, significantly lowering tail latency at the cost of slightly delayed activation of an optimized kernel. For rare long-lived workloads where kernel semantics diverge, the coordinator forces a swap within an SLAsafe window. - Complexity: added coordination code and a shim layer increases runtime surface area; mitigations include extensive unit and integration tests plus opt-in rollout via feature flags. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime.flags.atomic_kv_reconcile and runtime.flags.lazy_kernel_swap. Start with canary on Dedicated capacity group alpha, run for 72h, collect metrics (deferred_swap_attempts, reconcile_failures, tail_p99_latency), then expand. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] e2e reproduction [x] metrics and dashboards [x] docs and rollout guidance [x] feature flags and defaults off in Hosted. CI: initial CI run had a flaky scheduler test; fixed by reducing artificial timing in tests and re-running. Final CI status: all checks passed. Merge: squash and merge to main on 2026-02-25. Related: ENG-2891 (reduce tail latency on reconcile), ENG-3050 (kernel churn reduction)

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice approach; two questions: how do we ensure the shadow copy memory overhead won't OOM under large shard counts? Suggest adding a preflight memory cap.
Asha Menon: Added a preflight cap and fallback to streaming reconcile in low-memory cases; documented behavior in reconciler.go comments.
Lena Park: Need to ensure metrics emitted for deferred swaps are taggable by model and cluster. Also please add a unit test for shim passthrough on edge tensor layouts.
Asha Menon: Added tags model_id and pool_id and added shim layout unit test. Also added a small doc note about semantics.
Samir Patel: Approving pending one minor nits (log level and error text). CI flake was infra-related; rerun succeeded.
release_notes: Add atomic KV reconcile and lazy kernel swap to reduce tail latency caused by mid-flight kernel swaps. Introduces feature flags: runtime.flags.atomic_kv_reconcile and runtime.flags.lazy_kernel_swap. Backwards-compatible by default (flags off).
notes_for_operators: Default: features off. If enabling, monitor reconcile_failures and deferred_swap_attempts. In low-memory environments, reconciler falls back to streaming reconcile which may increase CPU overhead.
